references.text: God did not create the earth to be empty (tohu) – the same Hebrew word as in Gen 1:2 – but formed it to be inhabited
Jeremiah uses exactly the same expression 'tohu vabohu' (formless and void) to describe the earth in his vision of judgment and destruction
God's Spirit (ruach) sends forth creative power and renews the surface of the earth – parallel to God's Spirit hovering over the waters in creation
By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of his mouth (ruach) – God's Spirit active in creation
Uses the same Hebrew verb 'rachaf' (hover) about an eagle that hovers over its young – a linguistic parallel to God's Spirit hovering (merachefet) over the waters
The deep (tehom) covered the earth like a garment – parallel to the darkness over the deep (tehom) in Gen 1:2
By faith we understand that the world was created by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of things that are visible – reflection on creation from chaos to order
The earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God – parallel to the waters and God's creative activity in Gen 1:2
